basis: Pigmentary dermatosis with interferonopathy ancestry; torsion dystonia is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting neurologic involvement.
Carcinoma arising from epithelial cells of the renal collecting ducts.
Neurological sleep disorder with recurrent hypersomnia and cognitive dysfunction; photophobia and appetite changes do not establish other organ damage.
Microcephaly, developmental disability and skeletal dysplasia define disease; central hypothyroidism in 2/2; subglottic stenosis 30-79%. Microtia omitted under cap.
Purely psychiatric dissociative disorder without defined damage to an organ axis.
Clonal Langerhans-cell haematopoietic neoplasm; pulmonary location supported by lung-neoplasm and interstitial-lung-disease parents.
Skeletal dysplasia, hypotrichosis and immunodeficiency define CHH; neutropenia annotated 80-99%. Ocular and cardiopulmonary annotations omitted under the four-axis cap.
Substance-use disorder; alcoholic liver disease, neuropathy and other organ complications are separately diagnosed conditions.
Transient cerebral dysfunction from cerebrovascular ischemia defines the condition; no persistent neurological deficit or additional organ damage is required.
Progressive disease of multiple peripheral nerves; no defined immune mechanism or additional organ involvement.
Vasculitis affecting the arterial intima; vascular inflammation is the defining disease process.
Disease defined by a pathogenic inflammatory response affecting cutaneous apocrine sweat glands.
Neoplasm of breast parenchyma; breast has no axis. Metastases are not defining or common across this benign/malignant umbrella.
Ectodermal defects, cataracts and kyphoscoliosis define the syndrome. Dental defects, clefting and diabetes have unspecified frequencies, insufficient for additional involvement.
Cowden mucocutaneous hamartomas define disease; GI polyposis is common in Cowden (>30%), though subtype data are limited. Thyroid cancers are separate diagnoses.
Congenital shortening or hypoplasia of digital phalanges, sometimes with fusion and short stature; confined to the skeletal axis.
The syndrome explicitly combines oral clefting, intellectual disability and corneal opacity; no additional organ evidence supplied.
Iris pigmentation abnormality defines the concept; no evidence of additional organ involvement.
TAP2 antigen-presentation immunodeficiency; chronic skin ulcers and sinopulmonary disease are characteristic (>30%). Metabolic ancestry misclassifies the immune defect.
Skeletal dysplasia, cataracts and intellectual disability define disease; cleft palate is also a defining feature despite its occasional HPO frequency.
Optic atrophy in 18/18 with retinal/foveal dysfunction; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis. No extraocular neurological disease established.
Dementia caused by multiple cerebral infarctions; cerebral and cerebrovascular disease define the condition.
Fibrous dysplasia, pigmentary lesions and endocrine hyperfunction define disease. Phosphate wasting is typically FGF23-mediated, without intrinsic renal injury.
Lassa virus infection; most infections are mild or asymptomatic. Organ failure and permanent hearing loss do not meet 30% across all infections.
Focal autoimmune stiff-person spectrum disorder; rigidity and spasms reflect impaired neural inhibition, without established primary skeletal-muscle damage.
